subject: Cost & SLA follow-up: token volumes, unit economics, and latency trade-offs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fintechai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — token volumes and budget

Hi Alex,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking us through FintechAI's plans. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so procurement can evaluate options: 

Summary from our call:
- Primary use case: real-time personalized customer responses (chat) + nightly batch reranking for fraud alerts.
- Expected Q1 usage: 80–150M tokens / month; peak bursts up to ~12M tokens/day.
- Latency SLO: 200–300ms p50 for interactive flows; background rerank can tolerate higher latency.
- Security: will go through SOC2 + IP isolation (interested in Redwood Private for production).

Questions you promised to confirm for procurement:
1) Target budget range (annual or monthly) for inference spend.
2) Typical token mix: % prompts vs completions vs embeddings (rough).
3) Any firm SLO obligations for your SLAs/agreements (we can map to dedicated tiers).

Next steps from Redwood:
- I attached a pricing deck and a draft MAP (mutual-action-plan.xlsx) with two options: Hosted (tiered, usage-based) and Dedicated (reserved capacity + commit).
- I’ll send a short note on unit economics showing what $/1M tokens looks like across tiers and the latency trade-offs (streaming vs batched).

Please reply with the budget range and any additional vendor requirements procurement needs. Happy to jump back on a quick call if easier.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-pricing-deck.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fintechai.com>

Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — token volumes and budget

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few quick answers from our side: 

1) Budget: We're targeting $6k–$10k / month to start (pilot) with the plan to scale to $40k–$60k / month in production if results look good. Open to committed pricing for Dedicated if the unit economics make sense.
2) Token mix: ~35% prompts, 60% completions, 5% embeddings (mostly batch). Average tokens per transaction: 850 (prompt+response).
3) SLOs: Customer-facing chat needs p50 < 300ms, p95 < 700ms. We'll need an availability target (SLA) for production.

We reviewed the deck briefly. A few asks for the MAP: include explicit target $/1M tokens for each tier, and an option that shows streaming on hosted vs batched on dedicated with estimated latency and cost.

If you can send the unit-econ numbers today we can share with procurement and loop legal. We’re aiming to start pilot mid-Jan.

—Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fintechai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@fintechai.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 17:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — token volumes and budget

Appreciate the fast responses, Alex — below are the unit economics and the latency/cost trade-offs at a high level. I’ve also attached a short two‑slide extract from the deck for procurement.

Unit economics (target $/1M tokens) — illustrative:
- Hosted API (Developer Tier, streaming optimized): $650 – $900 per 1M tokens (best for low commit, bursty usage).
- Hosted API (Enterprise Tier, committed discounts): $450 – $650 per 1M tokens (requires monthly commit).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity, mixed batching): ~$300 – $420 per 1M tokens (includes reserved GPU cost amortization).
- Private / On‑prem reference: variable — typically similar to Dedicated once infra is provisioned; added onboarding & infra costs.

Notes on assumptions:
- Figures assume our recommended model family for chat with 8–12B effective params and quantization.
- Embeddings priced separately (we can show blended price if you want).

Latency vs cost trade-offs (practical knobs):
- Streaming (per-request, low-latency): best p50/p95 latency; higher cost since lower batching efficiency. Good for interactive chat where p50 targets ~200–300ms.
- Batching (micro-batching + async): lower unit cost but adds queuing delay; target when p95 can tolerate 500–1000ms or for non-interactive reranks.
- Continuous prefix/KV caching: reduces token billing for repeated context and improves apparent latency for cached flows.
- SLO-driven pricing: we map tiers to SLOs. e.g., Enterprise Hosted Tier guarantees p95 < 700ms for interactive path; Dedicated gives tighter p95 and higher throughput guarantees.

Concrete options for FintechAI based on your numbers (80–150M tokens/mo):
Option A — Hosted Enterprise (committed monthly):
- Commit: 100M tokens/mo -> est. blended $/1M = $520 -> est. $52k / month.
- Latency: streaming p50 ~220ms, p95 ~650ms.
- Pros: fast time-to-value, no infra ops; Cons: higher unit cost vs Dedicated.

Option B — Dedicated Reserved (6–12 month commit):
- Provisioned capacity sized for 150M tokens/mo with autoscale headroom -> est. blended $/1M = $360 -> est. $54k / month (but predictable and with better headroom for scaling).
- Latency: p50 ~160–200ms, p95 < 450ms with batching tuned.
- Pros: best unit economics at scale and stronger SLOs; Cons: commit + provisioning lead time.

Requested MAP updates: I’ll add a simple table showing target $/1M for each option and an estimated latency band for streaming vs batched paths. Also adding a DocuSign link for the MAP if you want to fast-track procurement.

Are you ok with me sharing the two pricing scenarios with procurement and legal? If so I’ll put dates for a pilot kickoff: engineering kickoff week of Jan 12, pilot run for 4 weeks.

Thanks — happy to walk through the numbers on a short call.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — token volumes and budget

Hi Alex — quick technical notes to pair with Marissa's pricing: 

1) Batch settings we typically recommend for your profile: micro-batches of 8–16 concurrent requests with request-level priority for interactive traffic. That gives a good cost/latency compromise.
2) Streaming + early-exit heuristics: streaming keeps p50 very low; we can enable token-level streaming on Hosted to meet the 200–300ms p50 for short responses. For longer responses we recommend streaming with a small initial prefix to reduce first-byte latency.
3) SLO-driven routing: we can route interactive traffic to a lower-latency pool (higher cost) and background rerank to a cheaper batched pool. This hybrid routing minimizes overall cost while preserving user-facing SLAs.

If you want, we can run a short latency vs cost projection based on your sample payloads (send a representative 10–20 request payload set). That will give a projected $/1M tokens across streaming vs batched configurations and show expected p50/p95.

I’m available for a 30min deep-dive next Tue/Wed to align infra sizing with procurement timelines.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
